content: The World Health Organization (WHO) published a guideline in 2016, identified by ISBN 978-92-4-154971-4 (NLM classification: WC 600). The WHO retains all rights to this publication. The designations and presentation of material within the document do not reflect any opinion by the WHO regarding the legal status of any country, territory, city, or area, nor do they address the delimitation of borders or boundaries. Any dotted or dashed lines on maps are approximate and may not represent fully agreed-upon borders. The mention of specific companies or manufacturers’ products does not imply endorsement or recommendation by the WHO over other similar products not mentioned. While the WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information in this publication, the material is distributed without any warranty, either expressed or implied. The responsibility for interpreting and using the material lies with the reader, and the WHO is not liable for any damages arising from its use. Regarding the involvement of experts in the development of the guideline, the following declarations were made: 1. Sheng (Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College, STD Control): No meeting restrictions, no involvement in related academic work, and no declared commercial or non-commercial financial interests. 2. Chesson, Harrel (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, USA, Division of STI Prevention): No meeting restrictions, no involvement in related academic work, and no declared commercial or non-commercial financial interests. 3. Cohen, Craig (University of California, San Francisco, USA): No meeting restrictions, no involvement in related academic work, but declared a related commercial financial interest. Specifically, he consulted on the development of new drugs for bacterial vaginosis with Symbiomix Inc. 4. Workowski, Kimberly (Public Health Agency of Canada, Centre for Communicable Diseases and Infection Control): Involved in protocol development for a phase 2 clinical trial of rifalazil for chlamydia treatment (US $4987) and reviewed efficacy data for a clinical trial of a chlamydia drug for Warner Chilcott LLC (US $10,640). These activities were related to the topic of the guideline. 5. Kiros, Mizan (Ethiopia, Disease Prevention and Control Directorate, Federal Ministry of Health): No meeting restrictions, no involvement in related academic work, and no declared commercial or non-commercial financial interests. 6. Latif, Ahmed (Zimbabwe, Public Health Consultant): No meeting restrictions, no involvement in related academic work, and no declared commercial or non-commercial financial interests. 7. Philippe Mayaud (United Kingdom, London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, Clinical Research Department): No meeting restrictions, no involvement in related academic work, and no declared commercial or non-commercial financial interests. 8. McCartney, David (United Kingdom, International Planned Parenthood Federation, Research and Technical Support): No meeting restrictions, no involvement in related academic work, and no declared commercial or non-commercial financial interests. 9. Mir, Ali M.: No further details provided in the text.
